hook: Is the key to eliminating neuropathy hidden within on a remote Greek Island?
claim: Nerve Soothe is a capsule sold for 'natural neuropathy relief'. Its story links nerve pain to diet and the long-lived people of the Greek island of Ikaria, and it calls itself 'the only product scientifically proven to stabilize' nerve symptoms.
ing_note: The sales page doesn't list a full ingredient panel in text; its references include a study of white mulberry (Morus alba) leaf extract, and the page refers to 'diabetes busting ingredients'. Check the label before ordering.
use: One capsule in the morning before breakfast and one in the afternoon, according to the sales page.
price_note: Prices are shown on the order page; the sales page claims it would cost $200 a bottle in stores and recommends ordering six bottles.
refund_note: The seller says you'll get a full refund even if the bottles are used.
checks: No supplement is 'scientifically proven' to stabilize neuropathy; that claim isn't backed by a published trial of the product.
Most neuropathy in developed countries is caused by diabetes, so tight blood sugar control is the proven way to slow it.
Supplements with some evidence for diabetic nerve pain (alpha-lipoic acid, vitamin B12 if deficient) aren't named on the sales page.
The Ikaria story describes a lifestyle (diet, activity, community), not a supplement.
cons: Full ingredient list not shown in text
verdict: Nerve Soothe makes a claim no supplement can honestly make and doesn't show its full formula on the sales page. If you have numbness, burning or tingling, see a doctor to find the cause (diabetes, B12 deficiency, thyroid problems, alcohol or medication); there are effective prescription treatments for nerve pain.
